keyVerseText: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
rootMeaning: The word ἀριθμέω (arithméō) derives from the root ἀριθμός (arithmós), meaning 'number' or 'a number as reckoned up.' This etymology highlights the action of assigning or reckoning a specific quantity or value to something, going beyond the simple English gloss of 'number' to emphasize the deliberate process of counting or enumerating with purpose and precision.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἀριθμέω appears three times and is translated variously as 'numbered,' 'are,' and 'number,' showing a consistent theme of counting or reckoning. This range of translation indicates its use both in literal counting contexts and in more figurative senses of accounting or reckoning individuals or items, underscoring the careful attention to detail and order in God's dealings with creation.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, ἀριθμέω reminds believers that God is sovereign over all details of life, meticulously counting and knowing each part of His creation. This verb conveys that nothing is overlooked or insignificant in God's eyes, reflecting His intimate knowledge and care. It reassures Christians of their value and security under God's providence, as He not only knows them but has them precisely accounted for in His divine plan. Such understanding fosters trust in God's faithfulness and His purposeful governance over all things.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 10:30 declares, 'But the very hairs of your head are all numbered,' using ἀριθμέω to emphasize God's exhaustive knowledge and care. The word 'numbered' here conveys that God meticulously counts even the smallest details of our being, symbolized by each hair. This highlights God's intimate involvement in our lives, assuring believers that they are never forgotten or beyond His watchful care.
